title: My Only Cry
author: Leila Ibrahim Semaan
summary: Since the atom bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1945), the world has filled with deadly weapons. In this free-verse (blank verse) poem, full title 'My Only Cry: Close the Arms Factories', a child speaks for all the children of the world and appeals to adults to stop making arms and wars.

The child asks, 'Who are you deceiving?' — adults ask her to speak to children, but she will also address the grown-ups. Being a child, she does not know how to lie like them. All the children of the world cannot rebuild what adults destroy, and a better world cannot be rebuilt without the adults.

Children's cries are useless 'in a deaf world' — adults do not listen. So she tells her friends not to talk of friendship, peace and fellowship; 'these words should be spoken by adults' — those who make wars must make peace. 'Enough promises. Enough waiting.'

She calls everyone to ask the adults to stop making arms, to stop making wars break out and to stop telling lies. 'We are sick, you are sick; but we are here.' In everyone's name the children ask: 'Close your arms factories and think about taming the winds' — use energy for peaceful, useful purposes. Right-wing or left-wing politics matter little to children; 'our life is essentially affection', but through the adults' fault 'a veil of dust lies over it'.

A powerful appeal for peace and disarmament; children's innocence and love versus adults' lies, politics and weapons. Written in free verse without rhyme, using direct address, repetition ('Enough promises. Enough waiting.', 'Listen, listen carefully') and metaphors ('deaf world', 'veil of dust', 'taming the winds').

sa2: The children cannot rebuild what the adults destroy through wars and weapons.
Why does the child call the world 'deaf'?
Because the adults do not listen to the children's cries for peace; their pleas go unheard.
What, according to the child, lies buried under a veil of dust?
The children's life, which is essentially affection, lies under a veil of dust because of the adults' wars and weapons.
What does the child ask the adults to stop doing?
To stop making arms, to stop making wars break out and to stop telling lies.
In 'My Only Cry', what does the child plead with the adults to speak about?
Peace, friendship and fellowship — the child says these words should be spoken by adults, who make the wars.
sa3: What is the central message of the poem 'My Only Cry'?

It is an appeal by the children of the world to adults to close the arms factories and stop wars and lies. Children cannot rebuild what adults destroy; their life is full of affection but is covered with dust by adults' weapons. Adults must use their energy for peaceful work and build a better world.

or: Why does the child say that words like friendship, peace and fellowship should be spoken by adults?

Adults make the weapons and start the wars, so only they can bring peace. Children's cries are useless in a deaf world; it is the adults who must keep their promises, stop the wars and bring friendship and fellowship.
